title: PREVIA: LLM ensemble predicts PTSD risk from emergency department trauma narratives
summary: In the journal abstract, PREVIA used trauma narratives from 145 patients at two New York City trauma centers to predict PTSD assessed one month later. Reported AUROC was 78.49% ± 5.75%, with precision 46.76% ± 8.66%. On 30 randomly selected patients, its performance was comparable to one PTSD-specialist emergency clinician. The authors describe these as initial findings requiring larger independent-cohort validation; prospective collection does not establish prospective evaluation of a locked model.
ai_technology: PREVIA clinically informed large language model ensemble
organization: New York University Grossman School of Medicine

evidence.tested: One-month PTSD prediction in 145 trauma patients; comparison with a specialist emergency clinician on 30 selected patients.
evidence.unknown: Abstract and metadata review only. Authors explicitly call for larger independent-cohort validation; full methods and timing of model selection relative to outcomes were not assessed.
evidence.ai_role: LLM ensemble extracts early post-traumatic stress symptoms, risk and protective factors from narratives and produces the risk forecast.
